name: Anonymous (Iroquois)
bio: The Book of Rites belongs to the Condoling Council of the Iroquois (Haudenosaunee) League, the public ceremony at which the nations of the confederacy mourned a deceased league chief and installed his successor. Its speeches, its hymn and its roll of the League's founders were kept in memory for generations before they were written down in the Mohawk (Canienga) language.

The texts in the archive were taken down by the ethnologist Horatio Hale (1817-1896) from copies held by chiefs of the Six Nations Reserve near Brantford, Ontario, one of them copied out in 1832, together with an Onondaga manuscript from the Onondaga Reservation in New York. He published them with his English translation as The Iroquois Book of Rites (Philadelphia, 1883).
